inferences: The component reading is 'WAL replay gate-and-replace caller': the window wraps the WAL replay orchestrator (PR #1932) with a ctx+0x140 gate, a helper-status check, and an object replacement whose +0x20 virtual call finishes the out status; source-level names for the ctx fields, the arguments and the 0xd0-byte object are not pinned
The status copy (phases 4 and 7) and the status move (phase 6) are distinct: the copy leaves the source intact, while the move frees the old destination message and zeroes the source

The second delete[] check in the move sequence reads the source message slot after that slot was zeroed, with no intervening write to it, so on a consistent move it never fires; it is recorded as an observed dead check, not as a live path

phases.name: gate
phases.rule: if the byte at ctx+0x140 is nonzero, out is set to code 3, flags 0, message null, and the function returns through the canary check; no allocation and no callee call happen on this path, and a pre-existing out message is not freed

phases.name: heap vector allocation
phases.rule: operator new allocates 0x18 bytes; all 24 bytes are zeroed, forming an empty vector (begin, end, capacity all null); the pointer is kept in r12 and in the -0x68 slot

phases.name: nonzero orchestrator status
phases.rule: if status1 byte 0 is nonzero, status1 is copied into out (code bytes +0..+5 and the message pointer; the old out message is not freed), the heap vector is torn down (see teardown), and the function returns

phases.name: status move
phases.rule: status2 is moved into status1: the old status1 message is freed with delete[] when non-null, then status2 code, flags and message are stored into status1 and status2 is zeroed; a second delete[] check then reads the already-zeroed status2 message slot and never fires on a consistent move

phases.name: nonzero helper status
phases.rule: if the new status1 byte 0 is nonzero, status1 is copied into out exactly as in phase 4, the heap vector is torn down, and the function returns

phases.name: object construction
phases.rule: operator new allocates 0xd0 bytes into r12; the -0x68 heap-vector slot is cleared to null and the heap-vector pointer is stashed in the -0x50 slot (dead after the phase 6 move); constructor callee 0x52144c0 is called with the register and stack arguments listed under constructor_call; rsp is restored by 0x20 after the call

phases.name: object replacement
phases.rule: the old object at *b_rcx is loaded; when non-null, its +0x8 virtual call runs; then *b_rcx is set to the new 0xd0-byte object

phases.name: heap vector teardown (stash)
phases.rule: the heap vector found through the -0x50 stash is torn down exactly as in teardown, using the stash pointer in r14

phases.name: virtual finish
phases.rule: the new object at *b_rcx is loaded into rsi and its +0x20 virtual call runs with (out in rdi, object in rsi); the callee's behavior is not pinned, but this call is the final writer of out on this path

phases.name: final free and return
phases.rule: the status1 message at -0x58 is freed with delete[] when non-null (it is not transferred to out on this path); the function returns out through the canary check

stack_layout.frame: rbp frame, sub $0x68 after pushing rbp, r15, r14, r13, r12, rbx

slots.-0x50: status2: code at -0x50, flags at -0x4c, message at -0x48; reused after the phase 6 move as the heap-vector stash
slots.-0x60: status1: code at -0x60, flags at -0x5c, message at -0x58
slots.-0x68: heap-vector pointer (cleared to null before the constructor call)
slots.-0x88: pointer to the -0x50 slot (set before the helper call; read by the cleanup entry at 0x520e7e4 and passed as the constructor callee's 7th stack argument)

status_layout.code_u32: +0x00; only its low byte is ever tested (the gate at phases 4 and 7); a code such as 0x100 passes the gate
status_layout.flags_u16: +0x04; copied verbatim on every transfer, never tested by this function
status_layout.message_ptr: +0x08, owning raw char pointer: moved (source cleared) in phase 6, copied in phases 4 and 7, freed with delete[] in phase 6 (old destination) and phase 12

teardown.array_free: when the vector begin pointer is non-null, sized delete frees it with size equal to vector+0x10 minus begin
teardown.element_loop: walk slots from begin to end in 8-byte steps; each slot's element pointer, when non-null, gets its +0x8 virtual call; null slots are skipped
teardown.rule: the heap vector is destroyed without resetting its fields; the vector struct itself is then freed with sized delete of 0x18 bytes
teardown.sites_shared: 0x520e972..0x520e9cb (phases 4 and 7, holder in r12); 0x520ea65..0x520eabc (phase 10, holder in r14)
